label: Special Right Triangles
overview: The two special right triangles — 45-45-90 and 30-60-90 — have fixed side ratios you can apply without trigonometry. Memorising these ratios lets you find any missing side instantly when you know one side and the triangle type. SAT questions embed these triangles in squares, equilateral triangles, and coordinate geometry problems.

keyFormulas.name: Finding any side
keyFormulas.latex: \text{Scale the ratio: if short leg} = a, \text{ then hyp} = 2a, \text{ long leg} = a\sqrt{3}

workedExamples.problem: In a 30-60-90 triangle, the hypotenuse is 10. Find the other two sides.

steps.title: Identify the ratio and scaling factor
steps.content: 30-60-90 sides are in ratio 1 : √3 : 2. Hypotenuse corresponds to '2', so the scale factor is 10/2 = 5.

commonMistakes.mistake: Multiplying the hypotenuse by √2 instead of dividing when finding a 45-45-90 leg
commonMistakes.fix: Hypotenuse = leg × √2, so leg = hypotenuse ÷ √2 = hypotenuse × (√2/2). Work backwards from the ratio.

commonMistakes.mistake: Swapping the 30° and 60° sides in a 30-60-90 triangle
commonMistakes.fix: The SHORTER leg is opposite the SMALLER angle (30°). The LONGER leg is opposite 60°. The hypotenuse is always the longest side.

quickTip: Draw the triangle and label the angles first. Then write the ratio 1:1:√2 or 1:√3:2 next to the sides. Match the ratio to the actual measurements by finding the scale factor (divide the given side by its ratio value).
